source_text: Sed iste, inquis, noluit nominare concupiscentiam carnis; tacet quia pudet, ac mira, si dici potest, pudoris impudentia nominare pudet, quod laudare non pudet [n99] . Displicet igitur tibi, quia novimus verecundiora nostra, secundum Apostolum, necessaria honestate velanda [n100] ; quia in hoc consilium sequitur Conditoris, ut quod ille in secreta corporis parte constituit, nos totidem verecundo operiamus obtectu.
pass_a_gloss: But this man, you say, was unwilling to name the desire of the flesh; he is silent because he is ashamed, and by a strange, if it can be said, shamelessness of modesty he is ashamed to name what he is not ashamed to praise. It displeases you therefore that we know our more shameful parts, according to the Apostle, must be covered with necessary honorableness; because in this it follows the Founder's counsel, that what he established in a secret part of the body, we likewise cover with a reverent covering.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: “But he,” you say, “was unwilling to name the desire of the flesh. He is silent because he is ashamed; and with a remarkable shamelessness of shame, if one may say so, he is ashamed to name what he is not ashamed to praise” (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.7.17). So you are displeased that we know, according to the apostle, that our less respectable parts must be covered with the decency they require (1 Corinthians 12:23). In this, our judgment follows the Creator’s: what he placed in a private part of the body, we likewise cover with a modest screen.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian contrasts opportunity/help with imposed necessity; load-bearing against natural compulsion to sin.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
